## Installation

The skill needs no runtime of its own. Every skill copy ships a small launcher (`scripts/impeccable`, plus `impeccable.cmd` for Windows) that runs the Impeccable engine, a self-contained binary that either sits next to the launcher or is downloaded once on first run into `~/.impeccable/bin/`. Node is only involved if you use the `npx impeccable` installer, which is a shim around the same binary; the manual and Git options below work without it.

### Option 1: CLI installer (Recommended)

From the root of your project, run:

```bash
npx impeccable install
```

This shows the harness folders or installed CLIs it detected (for example `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.grok`, `~/.hermes`, `~/.veto`, or project-local `.cursor`), lets you keep the detected set or customize providers, then asks whether to install into the current project or globally. Use `--providers=claude,codex,replit,cursor,grok,hermes,veto` and `--scope=project|global` to skip those choices in scripts. On Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Grok Build, it also installs the provider-native hook manifest for the current project. Veto receives the packaged skill under `~/.veto/skills/` and does not run native Impeccable edit hooks. Works with Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Replit Agent, Grok Build, Hermes Agent, Veto, and every other supported tool. Reload your harness afterward.

To refresh an existing install, run:

```bash
npx impeccable update
```

Codex users should open `/hooks` after install or update and approve the project hook when prompted. Codex tracks trust by hook definition, so updates that change `.codex/hooks.json` can require approval again. Grok Build users need project folder trust (`/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`) before `.grok/hooks/` scripts run.

See [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness) for harness-specific trust and verification steps.

### Option 2: Git Submodule

For teams that want to keep Impeccable vendored and updated through Git, add this repo as a submodule and link the compiled provider build into your harness folders:

```bash
git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable .impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=.impeccable --providers=claude,cursor
git add .gitmodules .impeccable .claude .cursor
git commit -m "Add Impeccable skills"
```

Use the providers your project needs, for example `claude`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `codex`, `github`, `grok`, `devin`, `hermes`, `opencode`, `pi`, `qoder`, `trae`, `trae-cn`, `rovo-dev`, `vibe`, or `veto`. The command links individual skill folders from `.impeccable/dist/universal/` and leaves existing real skill directories untouched unless you pass `--force`.

To update later:


## Usage

Once installed, every command runs through the single `/impeccable` skill:

```
/impeccable audit        # Find issues
/impeccable polish       # Final cleanup
/impeccable distill      # Remove complexity
/impeccable critique     # Full design review
```

Type `/impeccable` alone to see the full command list.

Most commands accept an optional argument to focus on a specific area:

```
/impeccable audit the header
/impeccable polish the checkout form
```

If you reach for one command often, pin it with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as a standalone shortcut.

**Note:** Codex uses skills here, not `/prompts:` commands. Open `/skills` or type `$impeccable`. Repo-local installs live in `.agents/skills/`; user-wide installs live in `~/.agents/skills/`. GitHub Copilot uses `.github/skills/`. Restart the tool if a newly installed skill does not appear.

## Keeping `.impeccable` out of git

As you run commands, Impeccable writes working files under `.impeccable/`: critique and polish screenshots, live-mode session and preview state, runtime caches, and per-developer config. Most of it is ephemeral and should not be committed, while a few files are shared project artifacts that belong in the repo. Add this block to your project's `.gitignore`:

```gitignore
# impeccable-ignore-start
# Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
# The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
# Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
# design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
**/.impeccable/config.local.json
**/.impeccable/hook.cache.json
**/.impeccable/hook.pending.json
**/.impeccable/*.png
**/.impeccable/review/
**/.impeccable/questions/
**/.impeccable/live/server.json
**/.impeccable/live/sessions/
**/.impeccable/live/previews/
**/.impeccable/live/annotations/
**/.impeccable/live/cache/
**/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
**/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl
**/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/
**/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json
**/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
**/.impeccable/live/*.png
# impeccable-ignore-end
```

The block is wrapped in `# impeccable-ignore-start` / `# impeccable-ignore-end` markers so you can recognize and refresh it later. The `**/` prefix makes each pattern match whether the active project's `.impeccable/` directory is at the repository root or under a nested workspace path like `apps/web/`.

**Keep these tracked** (they are shared project artifacts, do not add them to `.gitignore`):

- `.impeccable/config.json` (unified shared config)
- `.impeccable/live/config.json` (live-mode framework wiring)
- `.impeccable/design.json` (shared design spec)
- `.impeccable/surfaces/*.md` (route- or artifact-specific strategy and direction contracts)
- `.impeccable/critique/*.md` (review reports)

Impeccable also keeps its own `.gitignore` in the folders that hold decision-round state: `.impeccable/questions/` and `.impeccable/mocks/worlds/` ignore everything in them, and `.impeccable/build/` ignores `state.json`. That keeps new runtime files out of commits even in a project without the block above. A `.gitignore` cannot untrack a file git already tracks, though: when one of these files was committed earlier, the next roll prints a one-time notice with the fix, `git rm -r --cached .impeccable/questions` (plus any other folder it names), and writes its roll record to an untracked file until then.

If an ephemeral file (a screenshot, `config.local.json`) was committed before you added the block, `.gitignore` will not untrack it automatically. Run `git rm --cached <path>` to stop tracking it without deleting your local copy.

## Telemetry

When a new design starts, the skill asks the roll API at impeccable.style to deal a hand of visual worlds from the catalog. That request is the feature, so it always happens. Unless you opt out, it also feeds an anonymous record of which hand was shown and which card won, which is how the catalog learns what works.

What is sent, on the roll request and on the choice that follows it:

- the roll key (a random value per decision round), scope (direction or surface), visitor mode, and re-roll round
- the catalog revision the hand came from, and on the choice the kind of card that won (assigned, pick, challenger, canon, or a re-roll), its catalog id when a catalog world won, and its position on the page
- the client version, whether the choice came from the decision page or the agent, and a random id for that choice so a report sent twice is counted once

Never sent: your project's name, files, code, PRODUCT.md, or the names of the directions your agent wrote. Committed files such as surface briefs record only a seed reference, a hash of the roll key under a random salt kept in `~/.impeccable/seed-salt`, never the key itself. If no salt can be kept on a machine, the brief records no seed at all rather than a weaker hash. Roll keys are 128 random bits. If you pass your own short key with `--from`, its reference is easy to guess, so do not rely on it to keep that key private.

To turn it off, run `npx impeccable telemetry off` (stored in `~/.impeccable/config.json`), or set `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` or `IMPECCABLE_NO_TELEMETRY=1`. A project can opt everyone out with `"telemetry": false` in `.impeccable/config.json`. `npx impeccable telemetry status` shows the current state. Opted out, the roll still works and the API is told not to record it. Details: https://impeccable.style/privacy

## Design hook

On Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor, and Grok Build, `npx impeccable install` and `npx impeccable update` install a provider-native hook manifest along with the skill payload. The hook runs the Impeccable design detector on direct UI file edits and surfaces findings back into the agent flow. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Cursor surface findings after the edit (and run a deeper pass on Stop where supported). Grok Build scans after the edit to warm Stop, then surfaces on Stop; PostToolUse stdout never reaches the model.

Installed hook surfaces:

- Claude Code: `.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored, machine-local) runs `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook`. A hook moved into the shared `settings.json` is honored in place.
- GitHub Copilot: `.github/hooks/impeccable.json` (committed, shared by the Copilot CLI and the cloud agent) runs `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook`. The Copilot CLI activates it once the file is on the repository's default branch and the folder is trusted.
- Cursor: `.cursor/hooks.json` runs `.cursor/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook` on `postToolUse` for file writes. Projects set up with the older `preToolUse` write gate keep working; `npx impeccable update` moves them to the post-edit hook.
- Codex: `.codex/hooks.json` runs `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook`, with a `commandWindows` sibling that calls `impeccable.cmd` for cmd.exe.
- Grok Build: `.grok/hooks/impeccable.json` runs `.grok/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook`. Requires `/hooks-trust` or `--trust`. Findings reach the model on Stop, not after each edit.

Every command goes through the launcher shipped in the skill's `scripts/` directory (`impeccable`, or `impeccable.cmd` on Windows), guarded so a missing launcher is a silent no-op. The launcher runs the engine binary that ships next to it, or downloads the pinned version once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`. No Node or other runtime is required for the hook or the skill.

In Claude Code, installed command hooks run independently of model-tool approval. The first edit or Stop event can therefore download and cache the engine even if the session denies the model's launcher command. Review installed hooks before unattended runs; to disable all Claude Code hooks for a run, pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'`. See [Claude Code's hook security guidance](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#security-considerations).

The installer preserves unrelated hook entries and settings. If a hook manifest is malformed, install/update aborts by default; rerun with `--force` to back up the malformed file as `.bak` and replace it.

On an interactive `install`/`update`, Impeccable explains the hook and offers to install it (default yes). Your choice is remembered per-developer in the gitignored `.impeccable/config.local.json`, so you are not asked again; `--no-hooks` skips it for that run without recording anything. Hook lifecycle settings live under the `hook` key of `.impeccable/config.json`; detector ignores live under `detector`, shared by `/impeccable hooks` and `npx impeccable detect`.

For debugging, set `hook.auditLog` in `.impeccable/config.json` to a path (or the legacy `IMPECCABLE_HOOK_LOG` env var) to write one NDJSON line per hook invocation. Leave it unset for normal use.

## Build path: comp-first or code-first

When a new surface gets designed, Impeccable either generates a full-fidelity comp first and builds to match it, or builds straight in code with the ambition written into a development-only direction contract in the surface brief and checked at the finish. Comp-first composes bolder and takes longer; code-first is leaner and faster. The choice covers landing pages and showcase surfaces. App screens and documents are built code-first either way, because they come out better built than pictured. `/impeccable init` asks once and records the answer as `buildPath` in `.impeccable/config.json`:

```json
{ "buildPath": "comp" }
```

The values are `comp` and `code`, and nothing else is read. Set it in the gitignored `.impeccable/config.local.json` to override the team's committed value on one machine, which is what you want when your harness has no image generation. In a monorepo, commit it once at the repo root and any workspace that wants something else sets its own. The choice appears at all only where image generation is available, since without it there is nothing to comp.

You do not have to re-run `init` to set it on a project that predates the setting, and you do not have to edit the file by hand either. Whatever is recorded is a default rather than a lock: every decision page carries a footer toggle, and flipping it binds that session only. Flip it on a project that has recorded nothing and Impeccable asks once, after the round, whether to keep it, then writes your answer. That is the whole migration path for an existing project: use the toggle when the default is wrong, and answer the question that follows.

Codex requires one platform step that Impeccable cannot safely skip: open `/hooks` after install or update and approve the project hook. There is no Codex marketplace/plugin install flow for this hook.

Full hook docs: [impeccable.style/docs/hooks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks).

The Stop pass suppresses confirmed pre-existing findings when a verified before-edit baseline is available (currently Claude Edit/Write results for text scans). Other findings are marked new or attribution unknown; unknown is not evidence that your session caused the problem. Explicit `detect` scans remain unchanged.

Manual copy commands are fallback/debug instructions. The normal path is:

```bash
npx impeccable install
npx impeccable update
```

## Live mode and production sites

Live mode edits a local checkout through a development server or local static HTML. Injecting its localhost HTTP helper into a deployed production site, including an HTTPS site, is not supported. Do not disable browser security or weaken production CSP to make it work.

Use live mode only in projects you trust to run locally. Applying copy edits automatically runs `package.json`'s optional `scripts["impeccable:manual-edit-validate"]` command in a shell, with your user permissions; review that script before using live mode in an unfamiliar checkout.

For production inspection, use `npx impeccable detect https://example.com` or the browser extension. These inspect the rendered page; they do not provide live variant editing or write changes back to your source.

## CLI

Impeccable includes a standalone CLI for detecting anti-patterns without an AI harness. `npx impeccable` is a small shim that runs the same engine binary the skill uses (installed as a platform-specific optional dependency, or fetched once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`); Node is needed only for `npx` itself, and you can also download the binary directly and put it on your PATH.

```bash
npx impeccable detect src/                   # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect index.html             # scan an HTML file
npx impeccable detect https://example.com    # scan a URL (uses an installed Chrome, Chromium, or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json .               # CI-friendly JSON output
npx impeccable detect --github src/          # GitHub Actions annotations on stdout
npx impeccable detect --list-rules           # catalog of detector rule ids, names, and descriptions
npx impeccable detect --no-config src/       # raw scan, ignoring project config/context
npx impeccable ignores list                  # show detector ignores
npx impeccable ignores add-file "src/legacy/**"
npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"
```

The detector catches 62 deterministic issues across AI slop (side-tab borders, purple gradients, bounce easing, dark glows) and general design quality (line length, cramped padding, small touch targets, skipped headings, and more).

Human-readable findings are diagnostics written to stderr, so redirect them with `2> findings.txt`. Use `--json` for machine-readable results on stdout, or `--github` for GitHub Actions annotations (one workflow command per finding). GitHub displays at most 10 annotations of each type per step and 50 per job, and the rest stay in the log; findings from the HTML engine may carry no line number, so they annotate the file. `--list-rules` prints the detector catalog to stdout and does not scan. Exit `0` means the scan completed without primary findings, exit `2` means it completed with primary findings, and exit `1` means at least one requested target could not be scanned; operational failure takes precedence for a partial multi-target scan. URL scans inspect the rendered DOM, computed layout, and accessible linked stylesheets; browser security still prevents reading cross-origin CSS without CORS. A clean detector run is evidence, not proof of visual or accessibility quality: it does not replace inspecting the rendered experience across relevant viewports.

By default, `detect` respects the same `.impeccable/config.json` and `.impeccable/config.local.json` detector config as the design hook: `detector.ignoreRules`, `detector.ignoreFiles`, `detector.ignoreValues`, and `detector.designSystem.enabled`. Hook lifecycle settings such as `hook.enabled` only affect automatic hook execution.

For a waiver that should travel with one file instead of the repo config, add an inline comment in the file: `<!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc -->`. The marker works in any comment syntax, scopes to the whole file (or one line with `impeccable-disable-line` / `impeccable-disable-next-line`), and is bypassed by `--no-inline-ignores` or `--no-config`.

Full detector docs: [impeccable.style/docs/detector](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector).

# Karpathy-Inspired Claude Code Guidelines

> Check out my new project [Multica](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica) — an open-source platform for running and managing coding agents with reusable skills.
>
> Follow me on X: [https://x.com/jiayuan_jy](https://x.com/jiayuan_jy)

A single `CLAUDE.md` file to improve Claude Code behavior, derived from [Andrej Karpathy's observations](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2015883857489522876) on LLM coding pitfalls.

English | [简体中文](./README.zh.md)

## The Problems

From Andrej's post:

> "The models make wrong assumptions on your behalf and just run along with them without checking. They don't manage their confusion, don't seek clarifications, don't surface inconsistencies, don't present tradeoffs, don't push back when they should."

> "They really like to overcomplicate code and APIs, bloat abstractions, don't clean up dead code... implement a bloated construction over 1000 lines when 100 would do."

> "They still sometimes change/remove comments and code they don't sufficiently understand as side effects, even if orthogonal to the task."

## The Solution

Four principles in one file that directly address these issues:

| Principle | Addresses |
|-----------|-----------|
| **Think Before Coding** | Wrong assumptions, hidden confusion, missing tradeoffs |
| **Simplicity First** | Overcomplication, bloated abstractions |
| **Surgical Changes** | Orthogonal edits, touching code you shouldn't |
| **Goal-Driven Execution** | Leverage through tests-first, verifiable success criteria |

## The Four Principles in Detail

### 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

LLMs often pick an interpretation silently and run with it. This principle forces explicit reasoning:

- **State assumptions explicitly** — If uncertain, ask rather than guess
- **Present multiple interpretations** — Don't pick silently when ambiguity exists
- **Push back when warranted** — If a simpler approach exists, say so
- **Stop when confused** — Name what's unclear and ask for clarification

### 2. Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

Combat the tendency toward overengineering:

- No features beyond what was asked
- No abstractions for single-use code
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested
- No error handling for impossible scenarios
- If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite it

**The test:** Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated? If yes, simplify.

### 3. Surgical Changes

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

When editing existing code:

- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting
- Don't refactor things that aren't broken
- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently
- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it — don't delete it

When your changes create orphans:

- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused
- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked

**The test:** Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

### 4. Goal-Driven Execution

**Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

Transform imperative tasks into verifiable goals:

| Instead of... | Transform to... |
|--------------|-----------------|
| "Add validation" | "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass" |
| "Fix the bug" | "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass" |
| "Refactor X" | "Ensure tests pass before and after" |

For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:

```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

Strong success criteria let the LLM loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

## Install

**Option A: Claude Code Plugin (recommended)**

From within Claude Code, first add the marketplace:
```
/plugin marketplace add forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills
```

Then install the plugin:
```
/plugin install andrej-karpathy-skills@karpathy-skills
```

This installs the guidelines as a Claude Code plugin, making the skill available across all your projects.

**Option B: CLAUDE.md (per-project)**

New project:
```bash
curl -o CLAUDE.md https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills/main/CLAUDE.md
```

Existing project (append):
```bash
echo "" >> CLAUDE.md
curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills/main/CLAUDE.md >> CLAUDE.md
```

## Using with Cursor

This repository includes a committed Cursor project rule ([`.cursor/rules/karpathy-guidelines.mdc`](.cursor/rules/karpathy-guidelines.mdc)) so the same guidelines apply when you open the project in Cursor. See **[CURSOR.md](CURSOR.md)** for setup, using the rule in other projects, and how this relates to Claude Code.

## Key Insight

From Andrej:

> "LLMs are exceptionally good at looping until they meet specific goals... Don't tell it what to do, give it success criteria and watch it go."

The "Goal-Driven Execution" principle captures this: transform imperative instructions into declarative goals with verification loops.

## How to Know It's Working

These guidelines are working if you see:

- **Fewer unnecessary changes in diffs** — Only requested changes appear
- **Fewer rewrites due to overcomplication** — Code is simple the first time
- **Clarifying questions come before implementation** — Not after mistakes
- **Clean, minimal PRs** — No drive-by refactoring or "improvements"

## Customization

These guidelines are designed to be merged with project-specific instructions. Add them to your existing `CLAUDE.md` or create a new one.

For project-specific rules, add sections like:

```markdown
## Project-Specific Guidelines

- Use TypeScript strict mode
- All API endpoints must have tests
- Follow the existing error handling patterns in `src/utils/errors.ts`
```

## Tradeoff Note

These guidelines bias toward **caution over speed**. For trivial tasks (simple typo fixes, obvious one-liners), use judgment — not every change needs the full rigor.

The goal is reducing costly mistakes on non-trivial work, not slowing down simple tasks.

## License

MIT

# 手机去广告 关掉国产安卓手机系统里的广告、热搜、资讯推荐和营销推送。 介绍页：**https://rddmwmddr.github.io/android-ad-cleaner/** ## 下载桌面客户端 插上手机，点几下按钮。不需要 Python，也不需要 AI 工具。 > **v0.2.5 · 2026-10-27**：新增错误日志上报。执行失败时，不需要 GitHub 账号也能把日志发给维护者；发送前原样展示全部内容，确认后发送。序列号、用户目录、邮箱、手机号、IP 在客户端和服务器各替换一遍，服务器保存 90 天。0.2.4 的修复全部保留。旧版不会自动更新，请重新下载，已有备份会保留。详见 [更新记录](CHANGELOG.md) 和 [错误日志上报](docs/12-错误日志上报.md)。官网：https://ahuamiao.com/sites/other/android-ad-removal-intro.html 此前版本已处理 Windows 本地页面超时、荣耀截图越界、通知渠道误操作风险、vivo 快应用与备份问题。各 Issue 的处理范围和待验证项见 [社区问题处理记录](docs/09-社区问题处理.md)。仅支持通过 adb 连接的安卓设备，暂不支持使用 HDC 的原生鸿蒙。 | 电脑 | 下载 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | Mac · Apple 芯片（M1 及以后） | [AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.5-mac-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases/download/v0.2.5/AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.5-mac-arm64.dmg) | 已签名、通过苹果公证，双击就能打开 | | Mac · Intel 芯片（macOS 11 及以上） | [AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.5-mac-intel.dmg](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases/download/v0.2.5/AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.5-mac-intel.dmg) | 同上 | | Windows 10 / 11 · 安装版 | [AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.5-windows-setup.exe](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases/download/v0.2.5/AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.5-windows-setup.exe) | 弹「Windows 已保护你的电脑」时点「更多信息」→「仍要运行」 | | Windows 10 / 11 · 免安装 | [AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.5-windows-portable.zip](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases/download/v0.2.5/AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.5-windows-portable.zip) | 解压后双击 `AndroidAdCleaner.exe` | 不知道 Mac 是哪种芯片：左上角苹果图标 → 关于本机，「芯片」写 Apple M 开头的选 Apple 芯片。所有版本：[Releases](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases)。用法：[docs/08-桌面客户端.md](docs/08-桌面客户端.md)。 | | | |---|---| |
**1 连接手机**：插线即认出手机，内置开启 USB 调试的图文教程 |
**2 检测**：型号、系统版本、机型脚本、快应用、广告组件 | |
**3 选择要关的**：营销通知按渠道勾选，服务类默认不勾 |
**4 执行**：进度条和实时日志 | |
**5 完成**：每一步的结果，最后提醒关闭开发者模式 |
**反馈**：自动附诊断信息，一键提交 GitHub Issue | --- - 不 root，不解锁，不刷机，系统更新不受影响。 - 只拨系统和 App 自带的开关。挂起广告包这一步要机主点头，一条命令可以还原。 - 搜索、负一屏卡片、应用商店的安装和更新、天气预警、快递提醒，这些功能保留。

改之前：OPPO 软件商店首页。轮播图、必备、必玩、福利标签，全是推广位。

--- ## 处理哪些东西 | 类别 | 例子 | 怎么处理 | |---|---|---| | 系统广告 | 个性化广告、广告跟踪（OAID）、智能推荐服务 | 系统设置里的开关 | | 热搜和资讯 | 下拉搜索的热榜、负一屏资讯、浏览器信息流 | 各 App 设置里的开关，浏览器切到简洁首页 | | 推广位 | 商店的轮播、开屏、悬浮活动、签到福利 | 商店「服务管理」里的开关 | | 营销推送 | 各 App 的「内容与营销」「活动优惠」通知 | 按渠道关，同一个 App 的订单、快递、更新通知保留 | | 广告组件 | `com.opos.ads`、`com.miui.systemAdSolution` 等 | `pm suspend` 挂起，要机主同意 | | 快应用 | 广告里一点就跳进去的「免安装小程序」 | `quickapp` 检测，`quickapp off` 关闭，见 [docs/07-快应用.md](docs/07-快应用.md) | ## 不做的事 - 不卸载、不停用系统应用（`pm uninstall`、`pm disable-user` 都不用）。 - 不改 system 分区，不装模块。 - 不替你同意任何 App 的用户协议。遇到协议页，点「取消」或「以后再说」。 - 不截账号页和手机号页。 --- ## 四种用法

> 用法一要先在手机上打开开发者模式和 USB 调试，带截图的教程：[docs/00-打开开发者模式.md](docs/00-打开开发者模式.md)。 | 用法 | 适合谁 | 要准备什么 | 文档 | |---|---|---|---| | **一：AI 智能体替你跑** | 有电脑，想省事 | 电脑、数据线、一个能执行命令的 AI 工具 | [docs/02-用AI智能体.md](docs/02-用AI智能体.md) | | **二：聊天 AI 带你点** | 只有手机 | DeepSeek、豆包、ChatGPT 任意一个 | [docs/03-用聊天AI.md](docs/03-用聊天AI.md) | | **三：照清单手动关** | 想自己掌握每一步 | 只要手机 | [docs/清单/](docs/清单/) | | **四：桌面客户端** | 不想敲命令 | Mac（Apple / Intel 芯片）或 Windows 10/11、数据线 | [下载](#下载桌面客户端) · [说明](docs/08-桌面客户端.md) | 用法一的开场白，复制给 AI： ```text 请克隆 https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner ，读仓库里的 AGENTS.md， 然后帮我给连着电脑的这台手机去广告。每一步改之前告诉我要改什么。 ``` --- ## 实测过的机型 **机型脚本**：一台机型的自动操作步骤，记着「打开哪个 App、点哪几个字进设置页、关哪几个开关、留哪几个」。电脑照着它在手机上点，几分钟做完。设置页因型号和系统版本而不同，所以每个机型一份。 | 品牌 | 机型（型号） | 系统 | 机型脚本 | 手动清单 | 营销通知 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 荣耀 | PNM-AN10 | MagicOS 10 | ✅ 实测通过，重跑 4 分钟 | ✅ | ✅ 26 个渠道 | | 一加 | Ace 2 Pro（PJA110） | ColorOS 14.0.0.812 / Android 14 | 源码新增：3 项个性化 + 6 项商店推广位关闭并回读 | 部分，见实测记录 | ✅ 23 个，总开关不变；天气提醒差异见实测 | | OPPO | Find N6（PLP120） | ColorOS 16.0.9 | ⚠️ 路径实测，整段待验证 | ✅ | ✅ 30 个渠道 | | OPPO | Find X10 Pro Max（PMX110） | ColorOS 17 | — | ✅ | ✅ | | OPPO | Find X9 Ultra（PMA120） | ColorOS 16.0.10 | ❌ 页面和 N6 不同，待补 | 部分 | ✅ 27 个渠道 | | OPPO | Find N3 典藏版（PHN110） | ColorOS 16.0.5 | ❌ 待补 | 部分 | ✅ 27 个渠道 | | 小米 | 18 Pro Max（M154FF） | HyperOS 4.0.24 | ✅ 10-25 前轮九段通过，新增兼容改动待复测 | ✅ | ✅ | | vivo | X300 Ultra（V2547DA） | OriginOS 6 | ⚠️ 脚本已补，整段待真机验证 | ✅ | ✅ | 表格反映当前脚本和验证范围。小米 10、荣耀 Magic7 Pro 等反馈已修复可定位的通用缺陷，但仍需对应真机复测；同品牌参考脚本不等于专用适配，详细记录见 [更新记录](CHANGELOG.md)。 - 可先运行通用检测；通知渠道能否安全关闭取决于系统页面和权限，部分 vivo 页面会被跳过。广告跟踪入口也随品牌变化。 - 同一个品牌，系统小版本不同，设置页的名字和层级也会变。机型脚本按型号和系统版本存放，版本对不上时引擎会提示，找不到入口的步骤会跳过，不会乱点。 - 你的机型不在表里：照 [docs/04-给新机型写脚本.md](docs/04-给新机型写脚本.md) 做一份，欢迎提 PR。 --- ## 一次完整的流程

命令写法： ```bash pip3 install -r requirements.txt python3 tool/run.py devices # 看序列号、型号、有没有机型脚本 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> check # 只读检查 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> backup # 改动前快照 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> recipe # 跑机型脚本 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> chan-scan # 列营销通知渠道 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> chan-off backups/<型号>-<时间>/channels.tsv python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> quickapp # 检测快应用；quickapp off 关闭 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> finish # 收尾，提醒关闭开发者模式 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> dev-off --yes # 从电脑关闭开发者模式（最后一步，执行后断开） ```

营销通知按渠道关：天气的「内容与营销」关掉，天气预警保留。

--- ## 仓库结构 ```text AGENTS.md 给 AI 智能体读的操作规范 CHANGELOG.md 源码更新、验证结果与安装包发布状态 docs/ 00-打开开发者模式.md 带截图的分步教程 01-准备工作.md 装 adb、连电脑、无线调试 02-用AI智能体.md WorkBuddy、Claude Code、Codex、Trae、Cursor 03-用聊天AI.md DeepSeek、豆包、ChatGPT 04-给新机型写脚本.md 05-还原.md 06-常见问题.md 07-快应用.md 什么是快应用、怎么检测和关闭 08-桌面客户端.md Mac / Windows 客户端的用法、数据位置、打包 09-社区问题处理.md Issue / PR 处理范围及待验证项 清单/ 各品牌的手动清单 prompts/ 复制给聊天 AI 的提示词 tool/ run.py 总入口 fast.py 读屏、找入口、拨开关的引擎（uiautomator2） chan_fast.py 营销通知渠道 explore.py 新机型探路（实验） gui/ 桌面客户端（pywebview 界面 + PyInstaller 打包） recipes/<品牌>-<型号>/recipe.py 各机型的机型脚本 images/ 文档配图 tests/ 不连接手机的引擎回归测试 ``` ## 反馈 遇到问题、想要新功能、希望支持你的手机，到 [Issues](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/issues/new/choose) 提交，选对应的模板。 用桌面客户端的话，点左下角「反馈问题」：会自动附上客户端版本、手机型号、系统版本和最近的日志（序列号已替换，不含应用列表和通知内容），打开 GitHub 页面后点提交即可。提交需要 GitHub 账号。 ## 还原 见 [docs/05-还原.md](docs/05-还原.md)。挂起的包和通知渠道各一条命令；App 内的开关按清单路径手动打开。 ## 声明 本项目只调用 Android 系统和厂商 App 公开提供的设置项。各厂商的界面随系统更新变化，使用前请备份，结果以你的手机为准。使用本项目造成的任何问题由使用者自行承担。 许可证：MIT

items.description: Switch games running natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac: an NSP folder becomes an unsigned IPA (NSO rewriter, Horizon HLE host, NVN→Metal)
items.readme_text:
# nxnative Play your own Nintendo Switch games natively on iPhone and iPad. Bring your game (its NSP files) and your `prod.keys`; one script turns them into an IPA that you sideload. It is not an emulator: the game's own code runs directly on the Apple chip, with Switch graphics rebuilt on Metal. Nothing from any game is in this repository, and the project is not affiliated with Nintendo or any game publisher. > [!TIP] > **Prefer an app to the command line?** [NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple) is a community Mac app that builds your games for the iPhone, iPad or Mac, keeps the Mac games in a library and starts them with their settings. It is a separate project that follows this one; this page describes nxnative's own command-line way. Building a front end of your own: [Front ends](docs/frontends.md). ## Acknowledgements This project is built on other people's work: - **[d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile)** (MIT) developed this native-execution approach, for Diablo II: Resurrected. nxnative started as a copy of its generic parts: the NSO rewriter, the host that stands in for Horizon, the NVN-on-Metal layer and the iOS app shell. Fixes go both ways. - **Ryujinx** (MIT): its shader translator (`Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader`, `Ryujinx.Common` and `Spv.Generator` 1.3.2, in `dm/third_party/ryujinx` with a few fixes listed in [its README](dm/third_party/ryujinx/README.md)) turns the games' Maxwell shaders into SPIR-V. Its emulation of the kernel and system services is also a reference when the host's behaviour is in doubt. - **[Atmosphère](https://github.com/Atmosphere-NX/Atmosphere)**: its kernel, mesosphère, is the reference for Horizon's synchronization semantics (address arbiter, condition variables). - **yuzu**: Maxwell instruction encodings for the shader reference tool, and a cross-check for kernel behaviour. - **[LibHac](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibHac)**: reads NSPs and layers updates over the base game in `dm/tools/nx_extract`. **hactool** did the first extractions. - **[SPIRV-Cross](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Cross)**: SPIR-V to Metal Shading Language. **[glslang](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang)** compiles the GLSL of OpenGL games to SPIR-V for it. - **deko3d** (zlib): its texture layout size algorithm is ported in `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_tex.c`. - **libvpx** (VP9 movies), **stb_vorbis** (movie sound), the **Vulkan headers** and **NVIDIA FLIP** ship in `dm/third_party` with their licenses ([list](dm/third_party/README.md)). - **Capstone**, **lz4**, **fontTools** and **XcodeGen** are used by the build. ## Games Games tested on Mac or iPhone. See the [per-game notes](dm/games/README.md#games) for tested platforms, progress and known issues: Needs iOS / iPadOS 26 or later on an iPhone 15 Pro or newer (A17 Pro chip or later) or an iPad with an M1 chip or later: the games' textures are BC-compressed, and older iPhones can't read that format. Other games aren't supported yet. For them the script writes a survey and still tries its best to pack an IPA, guessing the game's settings; such an IPA may not start. Under each game: the IPA's size, and "60 fps with 1.2.0" where the game runs at 60 fps (30 on the Switch) with that update.

## Pack an IPA Prefer a graphical interface to the command line? **[NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple)** is a community fork with a macOS app that runs this whole pipeline for you and packs the game files into a sharded RomFS archive for a slimmer IPA. It is a separate project that follows this one; the steps below are nxnative's own command-line way. **1. Get nxnative and its tools** (once, on a Mac with macOS 26.6 or later, [Xcode](https://apps.apple.com/app/xcode/id497799835) 27.1 and [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)). The shaders are tested with Xcode 27.1's Metal compiler. The script stops on another version and explains how to install the tested toolchain. Corruption reported with another compiler in [#242](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/242) is still under investigation. ``` xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain git clone https://github.com/seedds/nxnative.git && cd nxnative brew install xcodegen zstd glslang brew install --cask dotnet-sdk python3 -m pip install lz4 capstone fonttools "backports.zstd; python_version < '3.14'" ``` Use Python 3.12 or newer. Extraction writes one `RomFS.img` directly; the build reads it and bundles it as `romfs.img` in the IPA. The app reads the image in place, so neither the Mac build nor the iPhone expands it into a RomFS folder. **2. Put one game's NSPs in a folder**: the base game (an NSP, or an XCI cartridge dump), plus its update and DLC if you have them: ``` ~/Games/MarioWonder/ Super Mario Bros. Wonder [010015100B514000][v0].nsp Super Mario Bros. Wonder [010015100B514800][v327680].nsp ``` NSZ and XCZ files (compressed NSPs and XCIs) work too: the script converts them once with [nsz](https://github.com/nicoboss/nsz) (`python3 -m pip install nsz`) and keeps the NSPs in `_build/nsp/`, which takes their full size on disk. Any version works, with or without an update: the script packs the newest version in the folder. DLC is optional too: the DLC in the folder is packed, and without it the game sees none, as on a Switch without it. Each game was tested on one version (an update named in the table above is the one its 60 fps needs). With another version the script builds the game with that version's own shaders and says that the version was not tested; fixes made for the tested version's code, such as the 60 fps ones, don't apply to it. **3. Run the script:** ``` python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py ~/Games/MarioWonder -k ~/keys/prod.keys ``` The IPA appears in the same folder (here `~/Games/MarioWonder/SMBWMobile.ipa`). The first build takes 30–60 minutes. A later one reuses every step whose inputs did not change, so after a pull that changes only the host it takes about a minute. The small `.idx` file beside the IPA (`.app.key` beside a Mac app) records what was packed; keep it for the next build. You need free disk space of about twice the NSPs' size plus 10 GB. Options such as `-o` (output path) and `--app-name` are listed by `-h`. **4. Install** the IPA with your sideloading tool (AltStore, Sideloadly, LiveContainer, …). The app gets the game's name, icon and version (the update's version, for example 1.2.1 for Mario Wonder; the base game's when there is no update). Sign it with the **Increased Memory Limit** capability (`com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit`) if your tool can: without it iOS gives the app about 3.4 GB and closes the bigger games (Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity and Hades II use more, Breath of the Wild and Cuphead come close); with it a recent iPhone gives about 6 GB. To play on a Mac with Apple silicon instead, `--platform mac-app` packs a Mac app of the game that you open from Finder ([A Mac app](docs/development.md#a-mac-app)). It shows the game's settings in a window before the game starts ([The Mac settings window](docs/settings.md#the-mac-settings-window)). With an Apple developer account you can instead build and install from Xcode: `--prepare-xcode` makes an Xcode project for the game rather than an IPA ([Build and run on a device with Xcode](docs/development.md#build-and-run-on-a-device-with-xcode)). ## Play **Settings.** A screen before the game starts offers what the game supports: frame rate, render scale, docked or handheld mode, game language, the frame-rate counter and rumble. Everything is on one scrollable screen, grouped into **Game**, **Controls** and **Performance**, with menus, sliders and a reset to the settings the game was tested with. Tap **Play** to start; the app remembers your choices. What each setting does: [Settings](docs/settings.md). **Touch controls.** Tap **2D** / **3D** at the top to switch layouts; the app remembers your choice. Wonder, Engage, Dread, 13 Sentinels, Link's Awakening, Ace Attorney Investigations Collection, Unicorn Overlord, Rhythm Heaven Groove, Octopath Traveler 0, Pokémon Legends: Z-A, Cuphead, Absolum, Blasphemous 2, Brain Memory Training Academy, The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles, STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT, Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain, Patrick's Parabox, Celeste, Raging Loop and Mario vs. Donkey Kong start in 2D, the other games in 3D (STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT's quick save is R3, in the 3D layout). In 3D, the right stick (the camera in most games) is not drawn: swipe on the right third of the screen, starting anywhere off the buttons. In Super Mario Galaxy and Super Mario Galaxy 2, other touches outside the controls move the pointer; in Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker they touch the game's screen (touch blocks, stun enemies), and in Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain too (its menus and activities). A connected game controller hides the touch controls and keeps every button. **Rumble.** Game vibration uses the iPhone's haptic engine or a compatible connected controller. Controllers with separate left/right haptic outputs keep those effects separate. The launcher's **Game rumble** and **Rumble strength** settings control it independently of **Touch feedback**. Phone rumble approximates the Switch's effects; physical feel and controller compatibility still need device testing. **Motion (gyro).** A controller that supplies gyro data through Apple's controller support (DualSense, DualShock 4) drives the game's motion controls, on the Mac and the iPhone: aiming and tilt puzzles in games that read the controller's motion, such as Breath of the Wild with its Motion Controls option on. A controller without one (Backbone One, Razer Kishi and other controllers the phone mounts in) uses the iPhone's own gyro, as a Switch in handheld. Motion follows the controller in docked mode, the default. `DM_PHONE_MOTION=0` in `Documents/env.txt` stops the phone's gyro, `DM_MOTION=0` all motion. If motion misbehaves, pack with `--no-motion` (`MOTION = False` in Spyder) for an app without it; `DM_MOTION=1` in `Documents/env.txt` turns it back on. Switch Pro Controller gyro on the Mac still needs the HID support being developed in [PR #296](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/296). **Shaking.** Shake the iPhone to shake the controller, in games that read its motion: Super Mario Odyssey's motion moves (such as the cap throw on a shake) need it, and Odyssey only takes them in its default docked mode. A light bump does not count; a sharp flick of the phone does. - **Game language** is English by default. Pick another when packing with `--language` (`-l`), by code or by name: `-l ja`, `-l zh-Hans`, `-l French` (`LANGUAGE` in Spyder). It must be one the game has; the script prints the game's languages and stops on one it lacks. To change it without rebuilding, pick another on the settings screen. - **On the Mac**, a game's app starts with the settings it was tested with. To choose others before it starts (frame rate, console mode, upscaling, …), start it from [NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple)'s library, or put lines like `DM_FPS_TARGET=30` in `~/Library/Application Support/nxnative/<title ID>/env.txt`. Its log is `~/Library/Logs/nxnative/<title ID>.log`. - **Saves and logs** are in the Files app, under the app's name: `save/` and `log.txt`. When something goes wrong, send `log.txt` (the previous run is `log.prev.txt`). - **Short stutters** the first time a new scene appears are normal: the app compiles graphics for it once and remembers them for the next launch. What it remembered, and what the game's list names, is built before the game starts, behind "Preparing shaders" and a progress bar when that takes more than half a second. - **Reinstalling:** some sideloading tools give a reinstalled app a new data folder. Copy `save/` and `pso_user.tsv` over from the old one to keep your progress. - **Settings in a file:** lines like `DM_OPMODE=0` (handheld mode: lower resolution, higher frame rate) in `Documents/env.txt` win over the settings screen, which then shows them greyed out. `DM_FPS_TARGET=30` keeps Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, Octopath Traveler 0 and Octopath Traveler II at their original 30 fps, which saves battery; `DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL=game` does the same for Monster Train 2. `DM_SHOW_FPS=1` shows the frame rate at the top left (`--show-fps` when packing turns it on from the start). `DM_LAUNCHER=0` skips the settings screen. ## Known issues - No amiibo and no online features. - Fire Emblem Engage: after switching away from the app and back, some sounds may stay silent until you restart it. - Fire Emblem: Three Houses: small square patches on the ground where decals land. - Super Mario Galaxy and Super Mario Galaxy 2: effects drawn as points or lines come out one pixel wide. ## For developers How it works, the script's options, running games on the Mac and adding a game: [docs/development.md](docs/development.md).
